map.name: The Gauntlet
map.testedVersion: Full static/source audit of current Drive artifact v1.0.2 + tester runtime feedback

bugs.title: Lethal Dropper failure can leave the client stuck after respawn
bugs.problem: A lethal fall in Level 6 can enter Minecraft native death/immediate-respawn while the Gauntlet also schedules its own Level 6 fall recovery. Tester runtime shows the player can return to the world with UI/input stuck and no usable movement or interaction until Minecraft is restarted.
bugs.expected: A failed Dropper attempt follows one deterministic recovery path and returns the player to the Level 6 recovery checkpoint with normal movement, UI and controls.
bugs.observed: Level 6 reacts to fall damage after damage has occurred and schedules custom teleport/vital recovery, while the world also has doImmediateRespawn enabled. Non-initial playerSpawn closes Gauntlet forms and returns without reconciling the active Level 6 run. In runtime testing, a lethal Dropper fall can respawn into a client state where movement and UI remain stuck until the client is relaunched.
reproduction: Enter Level 6 Dropper in an active Gauntlet run.
Fail the Dropper with enough fall damage to die rather than only touching the normal fail recovery surface.
Allow Minecraft immediate respawn and the Gauntlet Level 6 recovery logic to run.
Observe the player returns to the world but can become unable to move or use the UI/controls.
Confirm closing and reopening Minecraft restores normal input.
bugs.aiAnalysis: The failure has two competing recovery owners: native Minecraft death/respawn and the map's scheduled Level 6 custom recovery. playerSpawn does not reconcile non-initial respawns back into the active level state. doImmediateRespawn=true narrows the transition window and can contribute to the race, but changing that gamerule alone is not the preferred final fix.

relevantCode.reason: Contains Level 6 fall-damage recovery, entity death handling, playerSpawn handling, HUD/form cleanup and world gamerule setup.

bugs.suggestedFix: Prevent lethal native death during ordinary Level 6 Dropper failure. Detect the fail condition before death and immediately move the player to the Level 6 recovery checkpoint while restoring managed health/hunger/player state. Keep non-initial playerSpawn reconciliation as a fallback for unexpected deaths: resolve the active run/level, restore permissions and vitals, invalidate/re-publish HUD state, and teleport to the safe current-level checkpoint when required. Keep doImmediateRespawn only if the corrected single-owner recovery remains stable.
mustPreserve: Normal death handling outside the Level 6 custom failure path.

bugs.title: Player can fall and become trapped after Level 9 parkour is already complete
bugs.problem: Level 9 fall recovery is tied to the running phase. Once the parkour is marked complete, the recovery path stops even though players still physically need to traverse the normal Level 9-to-Level 10 door transition. A player who falls during this post-completion window can end up below/outside the intended route.
bugs.expected: Completing Level 9 keeps the normal door transition to Level 10, while any player who accidentally falls or becomes trapped after completion is recovered safely into the Level 10 entry area.
bugs.observed: Tester runtime shows a player can finish the parkour and then fall below before completing the Level 10 transition. The Level 9 recovery logic no longer owns that player after the level-complete phase.
reproduction: Complete Level 9 parkour normally.
Before entering Level 10 through the intended door, fall from the transition/finish area.
Confirm the normal Level 9 fall-recovery behavior no longer returns the player to a usable route.
Observe the player can remain below or trapped after Level 9 has already been marked complete.
bugs.aiAnalysis: This is a transition-boundary gap: gameplay state advances to Level 9 complete before physical player safety has transferred to Level 10. Recovery should remain defined until the next level entry is complete.

relevantCode.reason: Contains Level 9 running/completion phases, fall recovery and Level 10 transition logic.

bugs.suggestedFix: Keep the normal Level 9 to Level 10 door transition. After Level 9 completion, if a player falls outside the valid transition path or becomes trapped below the parkour area before entering Level 10, teleport only that player to a designated safe recovery position inside the Level 10 entry area.
mustPreserve: Players still enter Level 10 through the intended normal door path when no failure occurs.
Level 9 completion remains a single authoritative progression transition.

bugs.title: Level 15 boss and marksman entities can survive arena reset into a later run
bugs.problem: The general arena reset explicitly cleans Level 14 combat entities but does not own the Level 15 final boss and marksman-add cleanup. If a session ends or resets after those entities spawn, they can remain physically present while logical run state returns to idle/open.
bugs.expected: Reset, abort, completion and arena reuse remove every gameplay entity owned by the previous Level 15 generation before another run can use the arena.
bugs.observed: Level 15 has dedicated final-boss and marksman cleanup helpers, but the common arena reset path does not invoke complete Level 15 cleanup. Level 15 initialization removes normal wave mobs but does not provide an immediate general cleanup of a prior final boss/marksman generation.
reproduction: Use the developer workflow to reach Level 15 quickly.
Advance until the final boss and marksman adds are spawned.
Exit, reset or otherwise terminate the active arena session before the encounter naturally removes every spawned entity.
Reuse the same arena for another run.
Confirm old Level 15 combat entities can remain present until later Level 15 sequencing performs narrower cleanup.
bugs.aiAnalysis: Physical entity lifetime is wider than the common arena reset ownership. This can contaminate replay state and make the next run non-deterministic even though the run state has already been reset.

relevantCode.reason: Contains resetArenaRuntimeState, Level 15 wave/final-boss/marksman spawn and cleanup helpers.

bugs.suggestedFix: Make the canonical arena reset own the full Level 15 generation: remove Level 15 wave mobs, final boss and marksman adds using arena/generation-scoped tags before the arena becomes reusable. Reuse the existing Level 15 cleanup owner rather than adding a second cleanup path.
mustPreserve: Arena isolation across all six arena replicas.
Authored non-gameplay entities outside the active Level 15 generation.

bugs.title: Hunger can decrease during an active Gauntlet run
bugs.problem: Players can become hungry during normal gameplay even though hunger is not part of the authored Gauntlet challenge. This can remove sprint or otherwise change movement pacing during obstacle and combat levels.
bugs.expected: Active Gauntlet players keep a stable movement baseline with full hunger/sufficient saturation for the duration of the run unless a level explicitly uses hunger as a mechanic.
bugs.observed: The map restores health/hunger/saturation during level setup, but does not continuously maintain the active-run hunger state. Tester runtime confirms hunger can fall during play.
reproduction: Start a normal Gauntlet run.
Sprint/play long enough across active levels for vanilla exhaustion to accumulate.
Observe the hunger bar decreases during the run.
Confirm movement/sprint can become affected despite hunger not being a stated challenge mechanic.
bugs.aiAnalysis: This is not solved by a gamerule because Bedrock has no dedicated disable-hunger gamerule for this use. The active-run player-state owner should maintain the intended hunger/saturation baseline and reassert it after respawn/reconnect/level transitions.

relevantCode.reason: Contains per-level vital reset but no continuous active-run hunger normalization.

bugs.suggestedFix: Maintain full hunger and sufficient saturation for active Gauntlet players throughout the run, including after level transition, retry, reconnect and respawn. Restore the intended lobby/non-run policy when the player leaves the session.
mustPreserve: Any future level that intentionally declares hunger as a mechanic must be able to opt out explicitly.
Normal lobby behavior outside active runs.

bugs.title: Winning the full Gauntlet has no explicit final victory notification
bugs.problem: After the run is completed, players are returned to the lobby without a clear final Win/Victory acknowledgement tied to the terminal run result.
bugs.expected: The terminal run state provides an explicit player-facing victory notification or result acknowledgement before returning the player to the lobby.
bugs.observed: Level 15 can show a level-complete title, but the final run completion path resets the party and teleports players to the lobby without a dedicated final Win/Victory notification. Tester runtime confirms the completed run lacks a clear win notice.
reproduction: Complete the full Gauntlet through Level 15.
Enter the final finish condition.
Observe the party/session completes and the player returns toward the lobby.
Confirm there is no dedicated final Win/Victory notification for the completed run.
bugs.aiAnalysis: Level completion feedback and whole-run terminal feedback are separate semantics. The current terminal commit does not provide an explicit final-run acknowledgement.

relevantCode.reason: Contains Level 15 completion presentation and completeArenaPartyRun terminal reset/teleport behavior.

bugs.suggestedFix: Add one authoritative final victory/result acknowledgement after the run terminal result is committed and before lobby reset/teleport completes. Reuse existing run result/score state; do not create a second result authority.
mustPreserve: Automatic return to lobby after completion.

bugs.title: One timed-out arena can briefly pause maintenance for other active arenas
bugs.problem: Several maintenance/verification systems use a global any-run progression-blocked predicate. When one arena reaches a timeout-blocked state, unrelated active arenas can temporarily stop their own maintenance/verification until that global condition clears.
bugs.expected: A timeout or blocked progression state in one arena affects only that arena; other arena replicas continue independently.
bugs.observed: The shared guard evaluates all current runs and returns early for multiple systems when any run is progression-blocked, creating a short cross-arena coupling window.
reproduction: Run at least two Gauntlet arenas concurrently.
Place Arena A at a timed level and let its remaining timer reach the blocked/timeout boundary.
Keep Arena B active in a level that depends on periodic maintenance or verification.
Observe Arena B's guarded maintenance can pause while the global any-run blocked condition is true.
bugs.aiAnalysis: The impact window appears short under the current tick interval, so this is not a proven concurrency blocker. It is still a real isolation defect because arena-local progression state is used as a global maintenance gate.

relevantCode.reason: Contains isAnyRunProgressionBlocked() and the maintenance/verification systems guarded by it.

bugs.suggestedFix: Replace the global any-run guard with arena-scoped progression checks so each maintenance/verification task is blocked only by the state of the arena it services.
mustPreserve: Timeout handling for the affected arena.
Independent operation of all six arena replicas.
